title: One finite-precision improvement from a conormal splitting
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $t\in R$ be a non-zero-divisor, and let $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_d]$ with $d\geq0$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Let $J\subseteq P$ be an ideal generated by a finite list, and put $B=P/J$ and $M=J/J^2$. Define the $B$-linear map $\delta:M\to B^{\oplus d}$ by $f\bmod J^2\mapsto(\partial f/\partial x_i\bmod J)_i$, using the formal partial derivatives [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative]. Suppose that for an integer $r\geq0$ there is a $B$-linear map $h:B^{\oplus d}\to M$ with $h\delta=t^r\operatorname{id}_M$. Let $q>2r$ and let $a=(a_1,\ldots,a_d)\in R^d$ satisfy $f(a)\in t^qR$ for every $f\in J$. Then there exists $b\in R^d$ with $b-a\in(t^{q-r}R)^d$ and $f(b)\in t^{2(q-r)}R$ for every $f\in J$. No henselianity or completeness of $R$ is assumed.

source.place: Lemma 5.4.8, printed p.150, with auxiliary ideal I=R and the conormal factorization characterization (5.4.4); read online 2026-10-24; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag is asserted for this result.

proof.text: Let $\operatorname{ev}_a:P\to R$ be evaluation. By hypothesis $\operatorname{ev}_a(J)\subseteq t^qR$. Every element of $J^2$ is a finite sum of products $uv$ with $u,v\in J$, so $\operatorname{ev}_a(J^2)\subseteq t^{2q}R$. For each standard basis vector $e_i$ of $B^{\oplus d}$ choose $g_i\in J$ whose class in $M=J/J^2$ is $h(e_i)$; this only uses the definition of a quotient.

source.place: Gabber–Ramero, Almost Ring Theory, §5.4, (5.4.4) and Lemma 5.4.8, printed pp.148–150; agent-written elementary polynomial proof of the I=R, globally given conormal-factorization case; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: For every $f\in J$, apply $h\delta=t^r\operatorname{id}_M$ to $[f]$. Since $\delta([f])=\sum_i\overline{\partial_i f}\,e_i$ and $h$ is $B$-linear, this gives $[t^rf]=\sum_i\overline{\partial_i f}[g_i]$. The action of a class $\overline p\in B=P/J$ on $[g]\in J/J^2$ is $[pg]$; changing $p$ by an element of $J$ changes $pg$ by an element of $J^2$. Hence $t^rf-\sum_i(\partial_i f)g_i\in J^2$.

source.place: Gabber–Ramero, Almost Ring Theory, §5.4, (5.4.4) and Lemma 5.4.8, printed pp.148–150; agent-written elementary polynomial proof of the I=R, globally given conormal-factorization case; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Since $g_i\in J$, choose $u_i\in R$ with $g_i(a)=t^qu_i$. Put $c_i=t^{q-r}u_i$ and $b_i=a_i-c_i$. The inequality $q>2r$ ensures $q\ge r$, so $t^rc_i=g_i(a)$ and $b-a\in(t^{q-r}R)^d$. Multiplication by $t^r$ on $R$ is injective: compose the injective map $x\mapsto tx$ with itself $r$ times, with the identity map at $r=0$.

source.place: Gabber–Ramero, Almost Ring Theory, §5.4, (5.4.4) and Lemma 5.4.8, printed pp.148–150; agent-written elementary polynomial proof of the I=R, globally given conormal-factorization case; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Evaluate the relation of step 2 at $a$, using step 1, to obtain $t^r(f(a)-\sum_i(\partial_i f)(a)c_i)\in t^{2q}R$. Thus this expression equals $t^{2q}v=t^rt^{2q-r}v$ for some $v\in R$. Cancel $t^r$ by step 3 to get $f(a)-\sum_i(\partial_i f)(a)c_i\in t^{2q-r}R\subseteq t^{2(q-r)}R$, the inclusion following from $r\ge0$.

source.place: Gabber–Ramero, Almost Ring Theory, §5.4, (5.4.4) and Lemma 5.4.8, printed pp.148–150; agent-written elementary polynomial proof of the I=R, globally given conormal-factorization case; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Expand a monomial $\lambda\prod_i(a_i-c_i)^{m_i}$ by distributing its factors. Terms choosing no $-c_i$ give its value at $a$; terms choosing exactly one give $-\sum_i(\partial_i f)(a)c_i$ by the monomial derivative formula. Every other term contains at least two factors among the $c_i$, so belongs to $t^{2(q-r)}R$. Add over the finite monomial expansion of $f$. Therefore $f(b)-f(a)+\sum_i(\partial_i f)(a)c_i\in t^{2(q-r)}R$. Combining with step 4 gives $f(b)\in t^{2(q-r)}R$ for every $f\in J$, as required.

source.place: Gabber–Ramero, Almost Ring Theory, §5.4, (5.4.4) and Lemma 5.4.8, printed pp.148–150; agent-written elementary polynomial proof of the I=R, globally given conormal-factorization case; archival copy WANTED.
